FLAT: Ryosuke's ''Somewhere far' covers most of the planet.' is dry sarcasm, not his pedantry.

FLAT: Kohei's 'We'll find out on the floor.' is too polished; he gets cooler instead of shorter (top fix 1).

FLAT (minor): 'I eat my rice...' is a second tag; the lunch scene ends on two buttons.
FLAT: 'Nanoha said it as lightly as she knew how.' glosses the delivery (top fix 3).
FLAT: 'Natsuki laughed first. The moment closed up' repeats the on-screen laugh and names the mechanism; keeps 'it was fine' as setup for c1_0228 (top fix 3).
CUT: 'She did not let herself think about why...' explains the window image; interlude ends on stated subtext.
FLAT (minor): 'She's nice, Kohei. I like her.' repeats the interlude's decision and is generic.
FLAT (minor): 'longer than the garbage requires' repeats the c1_0076 construction; too neat or a tic.
FLAT (reader target): the callus as the last image before the dream points the dream at Natsuki (scene-level 6, top fix 2).
Scene-level 1: most exchanges still end on a neat button/topper.
Scene-level 2: feelings stated and narration vouching for the dialogue; the interlude is worst.

by.quote: Glossing is inconsistent: tsuka, shodan and 水 are glossed; fusuma, kinpira, karaage and taiyaki aren't.
The inline-gloss pattern repeats (see #10): "shodan (first dan)" in speech and "水 (Wednesday)" in narration. Three in one chapter makes it a house style, and it pulls me out of the voice every time.

items.why: Reader2 names four of the six terms as unexplained next to a gloss it calls helpful, so the obvious fix is to give more information; reader3 touches shodan but objects to glossing.

by.quote: c1_0227 > "Natsuki laughed first. The moment closed up, and it was fine." FLAT. It repeats the laugh already on screen ("Ha—") and names the mechanism: it's the sheet's "a laugh to close a moment" written out. Only "it was fine" is needed, as the setup for c1_0228's echo.

items.why: Same line and same narration-explaining family, but the diagnosis keeps 'it was fine' and c1_0228, the exact words the author cut.

by.quote: The text keeps telling me she's tiny ("Chibi," "needed the extra inches since middle school," slipping through "at elbow height"), and the picture doesn't sell that.
image_04: Nanoha's height difference is understated compared with the text, and she's adjusting the tie rather than folding the collar down.
The art shows her straightening the tie knot, flat-footed as far as I can tell, with her head at about his chin. She doesn't look like she needs the extra inches the text jokes about.

items.why: Readers point at the same height lines but blame the art for underselling them rather than the text for overplaying them.
No check flags the 'ironed by someone who meant it' line; the diagnosis keeps all of 1.4.
Nothing asks for a classroom reaction to Natsuki's looks; reader3's whisper suggestion is about Kohei's reputation.

by.quote: Kōhei has one move. The literal retort: "You're already in." "I'm standing in my own kitchen." "Meetings." "The pool is green." ... Each one works. Together they make him a setup machine for five different partners
Blur 2: Kōhei and Nanoha sometimes share the same dry register. "I'm standing in my own kitchen." and "The pool is green." could go to either.
But her absurd-logic bits overlap with Ryōsuke. "That's what it says in the minutes" could be his, and "'Somewhere far' covers most of the planet" could be hers.

items.why: Lines inside c1_0060-c1_0066 are cited only for a chapter-wide retort pattern or voice overlap; every check calls the banter itself good.
